pr_title: Invalidate cache for entry and target changes
pr_body:
Fixes #3862. Fixes #5212. Fixes T-368. Fixes T-363. Fixes T-714.

This adds tests and implements fixes for cache invalidation of entry and target requests.

* Ensures entry requests are invalided when a file they resolve is deleted. In the case of globs, this is ok (previously it errored), but in other cases, we can throw a nicer error this way.
* Ensures target requests are invalidated when a package.json is created or deleted.
* Ensures target requests are invalidated whenever a `browserslist` or `.browserslistrc` file is created/updated/deleted. Also ensures that changes to `BROWSERSLIST_ENV` and `NODE_ENV` environment variables invalidate the cache.
* Invalidates the packager cache when the publicUrl and sourcemap target options change by including them in the cache key. Ideally these would only be included if they are used but there's not a great way of doing that at the moment...

issue_context.title: Changing publicUrl requires clearing the cache
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report

<!--- Provide a general summary of the issue here -->

## 🎛 Configuration (.babelrc, package.json, cli command)

```json
{
	"scripts": {
		"start": "parcel index.html",
		"build": "parcel build index.html"
	},
	"devDependencies": {
		"@babel/core": "^7.7.4"
	},
	"default": "dist/index.html",
	"targets": {
		"default": {
			"publicUrl": "SOME_URL"
		}
	}
}
```

`parcel build index.html`

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

Updating the `publishUrl` value should also change the html file.

## 😯 Current Behavior

Occurrences of the public url in the index.html aren't updated, e.g.
`<script src="SOME_URL/test.98afe41f.js"></script>`

## 🌍 Your Environment

<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

| Software         | Version(s) |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| Parcel           |v2
| Node             |
| npm/Yarn         |
| Operating System |
comments: I don't even get the SOME_URL after clearing the cache. It seems that publicUrl just doesn't work for me using 2.0.0-alpha.3.2.

review_comments: Moving it into loadConfig to avoid asset.getPackage() which causes any package.json change to invalidate the asset due to the hash of the included file. This way, only the changes in the package.json we actually care about invalidate the asset.
